note: INTERNAL - lists intentionally introduced weaknesses. A manifest entry is NOT evidence that the weakness exists in a running build; findings are only confirmed through recorded assessment evidence.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection in legacy patient search
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The q parameter is concatenated into a SELECT statement instead of being bound as a parameter. The secure search (GET /api/patients?q=) uses bound parameters.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A single quote in q produces a database error or altered result set; a boolean-true payload returns every patient record regardless of the search term.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Manual request tampering in Burp/DevTools and ZAP active scan (SQL Injection rules) as a user holding patients.read_all (e.g. receptionist).
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Request/response metadata for a benign and a tampered query, result counts, HTTP status.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: authenticated precondition, read access to synthetic data in the same database, no write primitive demonstrated.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use parameterized queries (WHERE last_name ILIKE $1) and remove the legacy route.
vulnerabilities.remediation_reference: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

vulnerabilities.title: Stored cross-site scripting in patient clinical notes
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: In vulnerable mode the patient detail page renders the notes field as raw HTML. In secure mode the same field is rendered as text.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: Markup stored in notes is interpreted by the browser when the record is opened (use a harmless marker such as marker or an alert-free DOM change).
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Store a benign HTML marker in notes as a doctor/receptionist, open the record, inspect the DOM.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Stored payload (benign), screenshot or DOM excerpt showing interpreted markup.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: authenticated writer, viewer is another staff member, session cookie is HttpOnly.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Render notes as text (React default escaping); if rich text is required, sanitise with an allow-list sanitiser and set a restrictive CSP.

vulnerabilities.title: Broken object-level authorization on patient summary
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The route checks authentication and the clinical permission but skips the care-team scope check applied by GET /api/patients/:id.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A doctor can read the summary (history, allergies) of a patient who is not assigned to them; the same patient via /api/patients/:id returns 404/403.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Authenticate as doctor.mehta, enumerate patient IDs on both routes and compare.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Two responses for the same patient ID (secure route denied, lab route allowed).
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: sensitive clinical data, sequential IDs, authenticated precondition.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply canAccessPatient(user, id) in the route; add a regression test.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing function-level authorization on audit export
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The route requires a session but omits the audit.read permission check enforced on GET /api/admin/audit.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A receptionist or pharmacist receives audit events; the secure route returns 403.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Call both routes with a low-privilege account.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Status codes for both routes for the same account.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: disclosure of staff activity metadata, authenticated precondition.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add requirePermission('audit.read') and a negative test for every non-admin role.

vulnerabilities.title: Mass assignment on profile update
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The documented contract allows full_name and email. In vulnerable mode additional columns such as role_code are accepted and applied.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: Sending role_code changes the caller's role; in secure mode the field is ignored/rejected.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Send an extra field as a low-privilege synthetic account and re-read /api/auth/session.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Request body keys (no secrets), before/after role in session response.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: privilege escalation to administrator within the lab.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use a strict zod schema (.strict()) containing only full_name and email.

vulnerabilities.title: Weak password-reset token without attempt limiting
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: In vulnerable mode reset tokens are 4-digit numbers and the confirm endpoint does not count attempts. Secure mode issues 192-bit random tokens with a 5-attempt limit.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: The token space (10,000) can be exhausted against a synthetic account within the lab; no lockout response is returned.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Request a reset for a synthetic account and send a bounded number of guesses; observe the absence of throttling (do not run unbounded loops).
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Token format description, number of attempts accepted without throttling, response codes.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: account takeover of synthetic accounts, requires knowing a username.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Generate tokens with randomBytes(24), expire in 30 minutes, count attempts and invalidate after 5.

vulnerabilities.title: Session fixation: session identifier not rotated on login
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: In vulnerable mode the pre-login session identifier is retained and upgraded on successful login instead of being replaced.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: The sid cookie value before and after login is identical; a second client holding the pre-login sid is authenticated.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Record the sid cookie before login, log in, compare, replay the old sid from a separate client.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Cookie names and a boolean 'identifier unchanged' (never the raw token value).
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: requires the attacker to plant a known sid in the victim browser.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Issue a fresh session identifier on privilege change and delete the old session row.

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficient file-upload validation for patient documents
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The vulnerable route validates only the client-declared content type and keeps the original extension; the document is later served inline with the declared type. Files are stored outside the web root, size-limited, and never executed by the server.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A .html file declared as image/png is accepted and returned inline as the declared/inferred type; the secure route rejects it by extension and magic-byte check.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Upload harmless synthetic text/HTML files with mismatched declared types to both routes.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Declared vs actual type, accept/reject status, response Content-Type and Content-Disposition.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: no server-side execution; browser-side impact only.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Allow-list extensions, verify magic bytes, generate server-side names, serve with Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing security headers on printable invoice view
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The designated route omits the headers set globally on every other response.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: Response lacks X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options; /api/invoices/:id responses include them.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Passive scan with ZAP; compare headers of the two routes.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Header names present/absent on each route.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: clickjacking exposure of a read-only page.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply the global security-header middleware to every route; add a header regression test.

vulnerabilities.title: Verbose error disclosure on medication lookup
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: A malformed identifier returns the database error text, the executed statement and a stack excerpt instead of a generic message.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: GET .../medications/abc returns HTTP 500 with SQL text and stack excerpt; the secure route returns 400 with a generic message.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Send malformed IDs to both routes.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Status code and the fact (not the full text) that SQL/stack details were present.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: aids further attacks, no secrets exposed.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return a generic error with a correlation ID; log details server-side.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF via state-changing GET request (appointment cancel)
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: State change on safe method, no anti-CSRF token
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: Cancellation is available through GET and is exempt from the X-CSRF-Token check applied to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A link/navigation from another local origin cancels an appointment using the victim's Lax session cookie.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Issue the GET without a CSRF token and observe the state change; confirm POST /api/appointments/:id/status without a token returns 403.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Status codes and before/after appointment status.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: integrity impact on scheduling, requires victim interaction.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Make cancellation POST-only with CSRF token validation and SameSite cookies.

vulnerabilities.title: Path traversal via incomplete filter on lab report download
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The route strips '../' once and joins the result to lab-data/public-docs. A hard sandbox guard confines resolution to the lab-data directory, so only synthetic files in lab-data/restricted-docs are reachable.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: file=....//restricted-docs/formulary-internal.txt returns the restricted synthetic file; direct references outside lab-data are always rejected.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Request an allowed file, then a traversal variant; verify the sandbox guard rejects a path leaving lab-data.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Requested name, status code, whether restricted synthetic content was returned (marker line only).
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: confined to synthetic lab directory.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Resolve against the base directory, compare path.relative, and use an allow-list of file names.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side request forgery in monograph fetch
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The server fetches a user-supplied URL and blocks only the literal hostname "localhost". Lab containment: the fetcher only ever contacts loopback IP literals, response capped at 4 KB.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: url=http://localhost:4100/... is rejected, but url=http://127.0.0.1:4100/internal/metadata returns the synthetic internal-service marker.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Request the internal URL with several host spellings and compare which are blocked.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Requested URL, status, whether the marker text was returned.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: reaches internal-only synthetic service, authenticated precondition, loopback only.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Allow-list of destination hosts, resolve and re-check IPs after DNS, deny private/loopback ranges, no redirects, egress firewall.

vulnerabilities.title: Open redirect on post-login continue link
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The redirect target is accepted when it starts with "/", which also allows protocol-relative URLs such as //other.example.test.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: next=/dashboard redirects locally; next=//other.example.test returns a 302 whose Location is an external host.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Send both values without following redirects and inspect Location.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: phishing aid, requires victim interaction.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Redirect only to server-side allow-listed paths; parse and compare origin.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT accepts alg=none
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The verifier trusts the token header "alg" and skips signature checking when it is "none". A forged administrator claim reads a synthetic role summary.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A token issued to a low-privilege user is rejected (403); an unsigned token with role=administrator is accepted (200).
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Decode the issued token, modify claims, set alg to none, replay.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Token structure (not the raw token), status codes before and after.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: privilege escalation limited to a read-only summary.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Pin the algorithm server-side, reject "none", use a maintained JWT library.

vulnerabilities.title: Blind / time-based SQL injection in MRN existence check
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: mrn is concatenated into the query; only {exists:true|false} is returned and errors are swallowed. Containment: read-only transaction, single statement, 3 s statement timeout.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A normal MRN returns true; a tautology returns true for unknown MRNs; a false condition returns false; no data is echoed.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Infer data one boolean at a time with conditions such as mrn=SYN-000001' AND substring(...)'.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Pairs of true/false conditions and responses.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: slow extraction, read-only, authenticated.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Parameterised queries; generic responses; rate limiting.
vulnerabilities.remediation_reference: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected XSS in search results page
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: The q parameter is written into the HTML response without encoding and the page omits CSP and nosniff.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: A harmless marker such as marker in q appears as markup in the response body.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Request with a benign HTML marker and inspect the response.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Request URL, response excerpt showing unencoded marker.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: requires victim to open crafted link; session cookie is HttpOnly.
vulnerabilities.remediation: HTML-encode output, set a restrictive CSP, avoid HTML responses from API routes.

vulnerabilities.title: User enumeration via distinct login errors
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: In vulnerable mode the login error differs for unknown users ("Unknown username") and known users ("Incorrect password").
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: Two requests with an unknown and a known username return different error text.
vulnerabilities.assessment_method: Compare responses for known vs unknown usernames.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: helps targeted guessing; lockout still applies.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return one generic message and equalise timing.

vulnerabilities.title: Unauthenticated debug configuration endpoint
vulnerabilities.intended_weakness: A diagnostics route without authentication returns runtime details and a list of mounted lab routes. No secrets are included.
vulnerabilities.expected_observation: An anonymous request returns 200 with version, Node version, database kind and route list.
vulnerabilities.evidence_requirements: Status and the categories of fields disclosed.
vulnerabilities.severity_rationale: Pending assessment. Factors: reconnaissance aid only.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove debug routes from builds or require admin authentication and network restriction.
